summary.one_liner: ClamAV is an open source antivirus engine for detecting trojans, viruses, malware and other malicious threats.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes ClamAV as an open source antivirus engine aimed at detecting trojans, viruses, malware and other malicious threats. It points to external online documentation (docs.clamav.net) and a documentation source copy included in each release archive. It covers installation options: Docker images on Docker Hub, package manager installs, prebuilt Linux (Debian and RPM), macOS PKG and Windows MSI/ZIP installers, and building from source with a build options reference in INSTALL.md. It also links to signature-writing documentation, community mailing lists and a Discord server. The README itself contains no usage examples or API details.
use_cases: scan files for viruses and malware
detect trojans on a Linux server
run an antivirus engine in Docker
add malware scanning to a mail or file pipeline
how_to_run: Install from a package manager (see the online manual under "Packages")
Or download Debian/RPM, macOS PKG, or Windows MSI/ZIP installers from clamav.net/downloads
Or run using Docker (images on Docker Hub; see the online manual under "Docker")
Or build from source (see the online manual and INSTALL.md)
notable: Long-running open source antivirus engine with signature-based detection
Runs on Linux, macOS and Windows via official installers
Official Docker images available on Docker Hub
Unrar support is loaded at run-time so the GPLv2 core stays unlinked from the restrictive UnRAR code
caveats: The README points to external online manuals for most setup details, so the README alone gives little usage detail
Yara bundled code license info in the README is noted as out of date
RAR support depends on a separately loaded library; if it fails to load, RAR scanning is unavailable
